captions.detailed: A 3D-printable, pear-shaped plastic carabiner designed for use as a key ring. The body has a flat profile with bevelled, rounded edges along its top and bottom surfaces to make it comfortable to handle. One of the long straight sides features a diagonal, interlocking split-gap cut that allows the loop to flex open and closed.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, 3D-printable key carabiner in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to adjust the length, the two end radii (radius1 and radius2), the body thickness, the overall height, and the gap width for the flexible opening.
captions.factory: The code defines a 'swept_cylinder' helper module that uses 'hull' to connect two cylinders of different radii. A main 'loop' module creates the hollowed-out pear shape by differencing a smaller swept cylinder from a larger one, then applies a 'minkowski' sum with a custom 'diamond' shape to bevel all edges. The final model is constructed using boolean 'difference' operations to hollow out the interior and cut a diagonal, interlocking split-gap on one side using rotated cubes.
